message.content:
**Earliest non‑Christian historical references to Jesus**

| Author | Work (excerpt) | Date written | What it says |
|--------|----------------|--------------|--------------|
| **Flavius Josephus** – *Antiquities of the Jews* (Book 18, Chapter 3, Section 3) | ~93–94 CE | “James, who was called the Brother of Jesus, who was called Christ” (the passage also mentions “Jesus, who was called the Messiah”). |
| **Tacitus** – *Annals* (Book 15, Chapter 44) | ~116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.” |
| **Pliny the Younger** – *Letters* (Letter 10.96) | ~112 CE | Describes early Christians singing hymns to Christ as a god. |

These are the earliest surviving references that are widely accepted by historians as mentioning Jesus outside the New Testament.  
(There are earlier Christian texts—e.g., the Gospel of Mark (~70 CE)—but those are religious writings rather than independent historical records.)
